title: The food
description: What is cooked, what it is called, and how the name is built.
html:
THE DISHES

The dishes

IdeDishHow the name is builtWhat it is
nduonīIde Potato & Egg Skilletndu(ko) + onīServes 2. Potato peeled into paper-thin ribbons (so it finishes as the egg sets), with onion, tomato and scotch bonnet folded through; nothing left raw or runny.
nduanuIde Hot Pot Potatoesndu(ko) + anuServes 5-6. Parboiled then fried potatoes and separately boiled-then-fried boneless protein folded into a tomato-vegetable gravy. Chicken, beef, cow tongue, tozo or turkey.

THE WORDS

The words

IdeGlossEvidence
ndukopotatonduko – n. potato.
onīeggonī – n. egg. Etymology: From the Dura language.
anuanimal; meatanu – n. animal; meat
tozoa protein the recipe allows(a cow-foot/tripe dish, Nigerian usage)
